title: The Quaker Oats legacy: 150 years of innovation, nutrition and trust
summary: A look at the milestones, products and purpose that helped make Quaker Oats a household favorite. Learn more about the history of Quaker Oats.
body_markdown:
Throughout the 20th century, Quaker grew into a national brand and continued to innovate — adding puffed rice cereal to its food lineup in the early 1900s, and later introducing Life Cereal in 1961 and Quaker Instant Oatmeal in 1966. It would be another four years before the first flavored instant oatmeal, Maple & Brown Sugar, was introduced. Quaker Chewy granola bars followed in 1981.


In the 1990s, as consumer preferences evolved and Americans looked to labels detailing ingredients and nutrition facts, Quaker introduced the first food-specific FDA-authorized health claim for its oatmeal. The claim, which stated that “soluble fiber from oatmeal as part of a low saturated fat, low cholesterol diet, may reduce the risk of heart disease,” began appearing on qualifying Quaker products in 1997.


Over the years, The Quaker Oats Company expanded beyond oatmeal, building a portfolio that included ready-to-eat cereals, granola bars, pancake mix and syrup, sports drinks, pasta and rice products, and rice snacks. In August 2001, PepsiCo completed its merger with The Quaker Oats Company, bringing those popular brands into the PepsiCo family.
